term.def: A set of rules that decides what you see next in a feed or app. It learns from what you watch, like and click, then shows you more of the same.

prompt.prompt: Act as an AI risk advisor. My team uses [AI tool] for [task]. List five data risks, name who should own each one, and give one simple rule staff can follow for each.

quiz.q: TechCrunch reports that Facebook is giving users more control over their algorithm.
quiz.why: This restates the TechCrunch headline. It is about users getting more say in what their feed shows them.

quiz.q: Express Computer reports that a Trellix report says 98% of Indian organisations report AI-linked insider incidents.
quiz.why: This restates the Express Computer headline. It points to why data safety matters when staff use AI tools.

quiz.q: If an AI tool sounds confident, its answer must be correct.
quiz.why: AI can write fluent, confident answers that are wrong. Always check important facts, numbers and names before you use them.

quiz.q: You need to know coding to get good results from AI tools.
quiz.why: Most AI tools work with plain language. Clear instructions, context and examples matter far more than any coding skill.

quiz.q: Any AI tool is safe for confidential company data by default.
quiz.why: Privacy rules differ by tool and by plan. Check your company policy before pasting client, financial or staff data into any AI tool.
